content: If you use certain medications, such as diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting, your risk of side effects may increase. This medication can cause dizziness or drowsiness. The consumption of alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects, making you feel even more dizzy or drowsy. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are certain you can perform them safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar and/or alcohol. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, alcohol dependence, or liver disease. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly drowsiness, and are at a higher risk of dehydration. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. While this drug does pass into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking this medication on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Improper use of this medication, such as overuse or abuse, can result in serious harm, including a fast or irregular heartbeat or even death. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for longer than directed. Taking loperamide with certain other medications may also cause harm. This medication is used to treat sudden diarrhea, including traveler’s diarrhea. It works by slowing down the movement of the intestines, which reduces the number of bowel movements and makes the stool less watery. Loperamide is also used to decrease the amount of discharge in patients who have undergone an ileostomy. However, it treats only the symptoms of diarrhea and not the underlying cause, such as an infection. If you are using an over-the-counter product to self-treat, carefully read all the directions on the product packaging before taking this medication. Take this medication orally, usually after each loose stool or as directed by your doctor. Shake the bottle well before each use and measure each dose carefully using the provided measuring cup. The dosage is based on your condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also determined by age and weight. Diarrhea can lead to dehydration. Drink plenty of fluids and electrolytes to replace what is lost. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop signs of dehydration, such as extreme thirst, decreased urination, muscle cramps, weakness, or fainting. You may also need to switch to a bland diet during this time to minimize irritation to your stomach and intestines. Notify your doctor if your diarrhea does not improve after two days, if your condition worsens, or if you develop new symptoms. Common side effects of this medication include dizziness, drowsiness, tiredness, or constipation. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, remember that they have determined the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking loperamide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Antibiotics may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). Symptoms include persistent diarrhea, abdominal or stomach pain/cramping, or blood/mucus in your stool. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. This medication may worsen the condition. Loperamide may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs, such as diuretics, or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting.
